In this study, we investigate the emission of H$_2$CO and its link to disk properties, using a sample of 20 Class II disks in the Lupus and Upper Sco star-forming regions spanning over 1-6 Myr.

This paper presents a detailed study of the H$_2$CO emission in 20 Class II disks around 0.3-0.8 M$_\odot$ stars and tests how H$_2$CO emission changes with disk parameters such as gas mass, gas radius, dust mass, dust radius, stellar luminosity, and stellar mass.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.00128.L.
The analysis presented here is based on the AGE-PRO fiducial images, for two H$_2$CO lines in Bands 6 and 7.

Notably, we find strong correlations between H$_2$CO line luminosity and dust radius, gas radius, dust mass, gas mass, stellar mass, and stellar luminosity. This suggests that H$_2$CO emission is brighter for extended massive dust disks where H$_2$CO can form via CO ice hydrogenation on grain surfaces.

With only five disks with significant H$_2$CO detections in both lines, we cannot come to a clear conclusion on how H$_2$CO evolves with disk age.

all_quotes.quote: A natural first guess might be that larger disks provide a more extended emitting area, thereby increasing the integrated line luminosity. However, we find that the H$_2$CO emitting radii are only marginally correlated with the gas and dust disk sizes, which argues against the idea that emitting area alone is the dominant driver.
Since we only have two H$_2$CO lines, we expect higher uncertainties on our excitation temperatures than other studies that have detections toward more H$_2$CO lines.
With only two points in our rotational diagram, it is unclear how representative these points are of the total population distribution.

Additionally, in this work we only include the noise level in the channel maps when determining the flux uncertainty.
